definitions.gloss: sash; cord for tying back kimono sleeves; relay sash
definitions.explanation: A cord or band worn over the shoulders and crossed at the back to hold up kimono sleeves while working. Today it also means the sash worn diagonally by election candidates and the cloth sash passed between runners in an ekiden relay.

examples.english: To put on a sash (to tie back one's sleeves).

examples.japanese: ⟦{次|つぎ}→次：00819_tsugi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{走者|そうしゃ}→走者：21578_sousha⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{襷|たすき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}した→渡す：02442_watasu⟧。
examples.english: I handed the sash to the next runner.

examples.japanese: ⟦{候補者|こうほしゃ}→候補者：20439_kouhosha⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧{襷|たすき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かけて⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{演説|えんぜつ}→演説：01894_enzetsu⟧⟦した→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: The candidate gave a speech in front of the station wearing a sash with their name on it.

notes:
Often written in kana as たすき. In an ⟦{駅伝|えきでん}→駅伝：30715_ekiden⟧ the sash is the baton, so passing it on stands for handing a task to the next person.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {襷|たすき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧かける: to put on a sash
- {襷|たすき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{渡|わた}す→渡す：02442_watasu⟧ / {襷|たすき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧つなぐ: to pass on the sash; to keep the relay going
- {襷|たすき}{掛|が}け: wearing a sash crossed over the shoulders; diagonal
- ⟦{帯|おび}→帯：02610_obi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{短|みじか}し{襷|たすき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{長|なが}し→長い：00491_nagai⟧: too short for an obi, too long for a sash (neither one thing nor the other)
